newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans mixed, new crop up on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans mixed, new crop up on fund buying.

text.p: Heavy buying in November soybeans pushed that contract to sharp gains at midsession Tuesday, floor traders said.
"There's big fund buying in November," a trader said.
Rosenthal Collins bought eight million bushels November, Goldenberg Hehmeyer and Smith Barney each bought two million November, and Refco bought four million November.
July was under pressure as traders exited positions before first notice day on Monday, traders said.
"Everybody wants to get out of July," said one floor trader. "It's too volatile."
In addition to Monday being first notice day, the USDA also on Monday will release soybean stocks estimates as well as 1997/98 (Aug/Sep) soybean acreage data.
Selling in July was also prompted by Monday's sharply higher close. Traders characterized the close as "overdone."

Midwest weather remained bearish. Soybean growing areas were expected to have scattered rains and high temperatures ranging from 79 to 91 degrees Fahrenheit on Tuesday, according to Weather Services Corp.
At 1120 CDT, July soybeans were 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with other months 11-1/4 to two cents higher.
